lean.statement:
theorem wassersteinDistance_sq_le_phaseWassersteinSq
    [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [SecondCountableTopology E]
    {kappa : ℝ} (hkappa : 1 ≤ kappa) (mu nu : Measure (E × E)) :
    WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance mu nu ^ 2 ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal 6 * phaseWassersteinSq kappa mu nu
approved_definition_context: E is a real inner-product space. In the nonlinear phase declaration it additionally has CompleteSpace, FiniteDimensional, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace instances; the metric definition/energy comparisons do not assume these extra structures. Each theorem argument supplies its own parameter assumptions.

phaseQuadraticForm kappa (x,p)=(1/(2*kappa)+1/2)*norm(x)^2+inner_R(x,p)+norm(p)^2. phaseCost kappa (z,zprime)=ENNReal.ofReal(phaseQuadraticForm kappa (z-zprime)). phaseWassersteinSq is the infimum of the lintegral of phaseCost over all couplings of its measure inputs; it stores the square in ENNReal.

fderiv is the genuine Frechet derivative; gradient is its Riesz vector. ContDiff R 2 f is global twice continuous differentiability. Lagrange.basis is the true cardinal polynomial, sSup is real supremum, intervalIntegral is ordinary Lebesgue Bochner integration, Fin J indexes0..J-1.

WithLp2(E x E) has true Euclidean norm sqrt(norm(x)^2+norm(p)^2), with unchanged coordinates. The ordinary product norm used by WassersteinSpace is the default max norm. They are different norms; exact coordinate-sum energy is explicit in the metric comparisons.

The two coordinates of zeta are the two common vectors in the displayed numerical map. Each quantifier ranges over all points, with no noise-law/a.e. restriction. Real.sqrt is the nonnegative real square root. In the transport/moment declarations Measure/ENNReal integrability and inequality domains retain their usual Mathlib meaning; no actual sampler history is implicit.

WassersteinSpace.quadraticCost (u,v)=ENNReal.ofReal(norm(u-v)^2). WassersteinSpace.wassersteinDistance mu nu=(Transport.transportCost quadraticCost mu nu)^(1/2:R), with ENNReal real exponentiation; its square is the infimum of the quadratic-cost lintegrals over all couplings. For its E x E input the norm inside this cost is max(norm(x),norm(p)); it is not the Euclidean L2 product norm.
